name: HCP Waypoint
license: Proprietary SaaS (part of HCP, included with HCP Terraform Standard and Premium); the archived community Waypoint was MPL 2.0 up to its last release, 0.11.4
summary: HashiCorp’s hosted internal developer platform: developers create apps and add databases from templates that run Terraform modules in HCP Terraform.
intro: HCP Waypoint is a web portal and API on the HashiCorp Cloud Platform. It doesn’t provision anything itself: it drives HCP Terraform. Platform engineers publish Terraform modules as no-code modules in HCP Terraform’s private registry and register them in Waypoint as templates (a whole application, for example a GitHub repository with a CI workflow plus the cloud resources it deploys to) and add-on definitions (a database, a bucket, a cache). When a developer creates an application from a template, Waypoint uses a team token to create an HCP Terraform workspace from that module, sets the `waypoint_application` variable to the app’s name, and starts a run. The Terraform state, the run history and the cloud credentials all stay in HCP Terraform; Waypoint keeps the catalogue of templates, add-ons and applications. Installing an add-on later creates another workspace the same way, and the platform team can push template upgrades to existing applications.

For day-2 work, actions give developers buttons for operations the platform team defines. A custom action sends an HTTP request, with variables such as `${application.outputs.repo_name}`, to an API such as GitHub’s or a CI system. An agent action runs on an HCP Waypoint agent, part of the HCP CLI (`hcp waypoint agent run`), inside your own network: it connects to HCP Waypoint over gRPC with TLS and runs commands, scripts, Docker containers or HTTP calls against private systems. This is a different product from the Waypoint HashiCorp released in 2020, an open-source CLI and self-hosted server that built, deployed and released apps. HashiCorp ended that community edition in October 2023, archived its repository in January 2024, and rebuilt Waypoint as a SaaS-only platform for platform teams.
strengths: Developers get a new service, with its repository and infrastructure, from a form, without writing Terraform or waiting on a ticket
Templates and add-ons are ordinary Terraform modules, so the platform team reuses its modules, HCP Terraform workspaces and state
Template upgrades can be pushed to the applications already created from that template
Actions put rollbacks, builds and feature flags behind one button, and agents reach systems in private or on-premises networks
limits: SaaS only: there is no self-managed edition since the community edition ended, and every agent must authenticate to HCP
Not sold alone: it needs an HCP Terraform organization on the Standard edition or higher, for no-code modules and the private registry
It doesn’t build or deploy code itself; CI/CD stays in GitHub Actions or similar, and Waypoint only triggers it through actions
Agents receive every variable of the actions they run, sensitive ones decrypted, so the agent host is as sensitive as those secrets
Nothing carries over from community Waypoint: `waypoint.hcl` files and `waypoint up` workflows have no equivalent

story: By 2020, shipping an app meant learning containers, schedulers, YAML files and serverless platforms, each with its own tool: Docker and `kubectl` for Kubernetes, Packer and Terraform for VMs, a separate CLI for each serverless platform. On October 15, 2020, Mitchell Hashimoto announced Waypoint, an open-source project that gave developers one workflow to build, deploy and release on any platform. A `waypoint.hcl` file described the app, `waypoint up` did all three steps, and every deployment got a public `waypoint.run` URL with a TLS certificate, plus logs and `waypoint exec`.

For many operators, setting up a reliable and secure Waypoint server was a barrier to even trying it, so in 2022 HashiCorp offered it as a managed service, HCP Waypoint, first as a private beta in June and a public beta in October, with runners on the customer’s own infrastructure. In October 2023 HashiCorp changed course: Waypoint would be re-architected as a SaaS-only product for platform teams, built on Terraform, and active development of the community edition ended. Its repository was archived in January 2024. HCP Waypoint, with templates and add-ons, became generally available in October 2024, and actions followed in June 2025.

choices.choice: One workflow on top of existing platforms
choices.why: Waypoint didn’t replace Kubernetes, Nomad or CI systems. Plugins handled each platform, so the same build, deploy and release steps worked whether an app ran on Kubernetes, ECS or Cloud Run.

choices.choice: A hosted server instead of a self-hosted one
choices.why: Setting up a reliable, secure Waypoint server kept operators from trying Waypoint at all. HCP Waypoint took that work away, and the 2023 redesign went further and dropped the self-hosted edition.

For the 2023 redesign, HashiCorp moved the focus from deploying code to letting platform teams package infrastructure, dependencies and workflows. Terraform modules already described that infrastructure, so templates and add-ons reuse them.

timeline.text: Waypoint 0.1 released as open source on October 15
HCP Waypoint private beta in June, public beta in October
HashiCorp ends the community edition in October and goes SaaS-only
Community repository archived in January; HCP Waypoint generally available in October
HCP Waypoint actions generally available in June
